title: AI with Authority, from Application to Silicon
abstract: For sixty years, machine verification has been a major cost overhead, affordable only for exceptional artifacts. Here we report that generative AI inverts this relationship: at AI speed, machine verification is not only economical but essential to productivity --- it is the incorruptible referee that lets one person safely direct autonomous machine work at scale. In five weeks, one researcher on consumer AI subscriptions directed a small fleet of AI agents from application code, through a verified compiler and executive, to a RISC-V processor taped out on a community silicon shuttle; no proof passed through human review, and no RTL was written by a human. The working discipline --- the Salt method --- rests on a proof kernel no hallucinated proof can pass: mathematical claims travel between agents as kernel-checked artifacts, and human attention is reserved for statements, designs, and rulings. Verification is stated link by link, from the Lean 4 kernel to SAT-checked equivalence at the silicon boundary. We publish the complete accounting: theorem provenance, a pre-registered token meter, floor-bounded human time, and an error ledger whose catch numbering runs to #256 --- a monotone counter over the mathematics campaign's append-only flags ledger, maintained 2026-07-07 to 2026-07-20 (one number, #79, was never assigned; later catches are recorded un-numbered) --- against zero incorrect proofs reaching the record.
title_zh: 具有权威性的人工智能：从应用到硅片
abstract_zh: 六十年来，机器验证一直是一个主要的成本开销，仅对特殊的人工制品才负担得起。本文报告了生成式人工智能颠覆了这一关系：在人工智能的速度下，机器验证不仅经济实惠，而且对生产力至关重要——它是不可腐败的裁判，使得一个人能够安全地大规模指挥自主机器工作。在五周内，一名研究人员通过消费者人工智能订阅服务指挥了一小队人工智能代理，从应用代码、经过验证的编译器和执行器，到在社区硅片班车上完成的RISC-V处理器；没有任何证明经过人工审查，也没有任何RTL由人类编写。这种工作方法——Salt方法——基于一个证明内核，任何虚假的证明都无法通过：数学声明在代理之间以内核验证的人工制品形式传递，而人类的注意力仅保留给声明、设计和裁决。验证逐环节陈述，从Lean 4内核到硅片边界的SAT验证等价性。我们发布了完整的记录：定理来源、预注册的令牌计量器、最低限度的人类时间，以及错误日志，其捕获编号达到#256——一个数学活动的追加式标志日志中的单调计数器，维护时间为2026年7月7日至2026年7月20日（编号#79未被分配；后续捕获未编号）——没有任何错误证明进入记录。

title: Assessing Triple Modular Redundancy for Wide-Link, Low-Latency NoC Routers: Reliability and Physical Design Challenges
authors: Chen Wu, Michael Rogenmoser, Luca Benini, Angelo Garofalo
abstract: Protecting the Network-on-Chip (NoC) of physical-AI tile-based accelerators deployed in harsh environments against single-event effects (SEEs) is paramount for preventing NoC failures that can lead to deadlocks and silent data corruption (SDC). Prior work on reliable NoCs has largely focused on narrow links (e.g., 32-bit), deeply pipelined routers, and single-event upsets (SEUs). However, the state of the art has evolved toward low-latency NoC routers with ultra-wide links, implemented on advanced technology nodes and operating at frequencies above 1 GHz. We evaluate the cost and reliability trade-offs of implementing Triple Modular Redundancy (TMR) at three granularities (coarse, state-only, and full) for a 2-cycle-latency NoC router with 512-bit wide links. We carry out RTL-to-GDSII physical design in TSMC 7nm technology, as well as both RTL- and netlist-level SEU and SET fault injection campaigns. We evaluate the three TMR approaches in terms of reliability, cost, and physical design strategies, further extending the assessment from a standalone router to a full AI acceleration tile. Our results show that state-only and coarse-grained TMR do not provide sufficient protection against SEEs, whereas full TMR eliminates all observed failures across more than one million injected faults per experiment. Although the standalone full-TMR router incurs a 7.04x area overhead, this cost is drastically amortized once integrated into a complete AI accelerator tile with processors and local L1 memories: the same design adds only 16.8% area and 15.2% power consumption under a GEMM benchmark at the system level, with the critical path of the tile entirely unaffected. These results demonstrate that advanced technology nodes provide sufficient routing capacity to make full TMR a practical and deployable solution for protecting NoCs in Physical AI systems operating in harsh environments.
title_zh: 评估宽链路、低延迟NoC路由器的三模冗余：可靠性与物理设计挑战
abstract_zh: 在恶劣环境中部署的基于物理AI的瓦片式加速器，其片上网络（NoC）需要防护单事件效应（SEE），以防止NoC故障导致死锁和静默数据损坏（SDC）。以往关于可靠NoC的研究主要集中在窄链路（例如32位）、深度流水线路由器以及单事件翻转（SEU）。然而，当前技术已发展至具有超宽链路、低延迟的NoC路由器，这些路由器采用先进工艺节点并运行在超过1 GHz的频率下。我们评估了在三种粒度（粗粒度、仅状态保护和全保护）下实现三模冗余（TMR）的成本与可靠性权衡，针对一个具有512位宽链路、2周期延迟的NoC路由器进行研究。我们在台积电7nm技术节点上完成了从RTL到GDSII的物理设计，并进行了RTL级和网表级的SEU和SET故障注入实验。我们从可靠性、成本和物理设计策略方面评估了三种TMR方法，并将评估范围从单独的路由器扩展到完整的AI加速瓦片。结果表明，仅状态保护和粗粒度TMR无法提供足够的SEE防护，而全保护TMR在每次实验中注入超过一百万次故障后完全消除了所有观察到的故障。尽管单独的全TMR路由器带来了7.04倍的面积开销，但一旦集成到包含处理器和本地L1存储器的完整AI加速瓦片中，这一成本显著摊薄：在系统级别的GEMM基准测试下，该设计仅增加了16.8%的面积和15.2%的功耗，同时瓦片的关键路径完全不受影响。这些结果表明，先进工艺节点提供了足够的布线能力，使全TMR成为保护运行于恶劣环境中的物理AI系统中的NoC的实用且可部署的解决方案。
